name: Offline Cheap Text LLM Gemma 4
tagline: EXPERIMENTAL, and the SLOWEST of the three — many minutes per answer. Google's Gemma 4, entirely on your device.
description:
⚠ EXPERIMENTAL — PLEASE READ THIS BEFORE YOU INSTALL

This is a demonstration, not an everyday assistant. It exists to prove a real language model can live in an app, run on your device, and answer with nothing leaving. Judged as a chat assistant, its speed is NOT ACCEPTABLE for common use — and it is not trying to be. Install it to watch the thing work, not to get work done.

HOW SLOW, CONCRETELY. It can only use one processor core, so the model writes at about the pace of slow typing. Measured on a phone, one of these three took 362 seconds — six minutes — to answer a single ordinary question. This one is the SLOWEST of the three. On a desktop it is better, and still far slower than any hosted model you have used. The FIRST answer of a session is slower again, because it loads the model before writing a word.

WHAT IT COSTS BEFORE IT SAYS ANYTHING: a 1.75 GB download, kept on this device.

WHAT YOU GET FOR THAT: privacy that is structural rather than promised. No account, no key, no way out to the internet — not "we don't look", but "there is nowhere for it to go". If that is what you came for, it is worth the wait. If you want a fast, capable assistant, leave this uninstalled and point Settings → AI models → Cheapest text LLM at a hosted service instead; every app that asks for cheap text will use that, and answer in seconds.

———

This is a model other apps can use. Install it, keep it in your Providers folder, and assign it to Cheapest text LLM in Settings → AI models. From then on, every app that asks the computer for cheap text — Ask AI, Chat drafts, game hints — is answered on this device. No account, no key, nothing leaves your device.

The model is Google's Gemma 4 E2B — downloaded once at install (~1.75 GB, checked against a fingerprint baked into the app) and kept on this device.

WHY THIS ONE: the model itself is Apache-2.0. That is a real open-source licence with no use restrictions — unlike Gemma 3, whose model ships under Google's Gemma Terms of Use. If the licence on the model matters to you, this is the one to pick.

WHAT IT COSTS YOU: it is the biggest download of the three (1.75 GB, against Gemma 3's 769 MB and BitNet's 1.03 GB) and the slowest to answer. Gemma 3 is the one to pick for speed; BitNet is the other alternative. All three do the same job — install any or all and switch in Settings.

Gemma 4 can "think out loud" before answering, but this app turns that off: the answer is what you want, and every extra word is time you wait.

A built-in tiny self-test model proves the pipeline instantly (clearly labeled — it speaks nonsense, not answers) while the real model downloads.
